items.title: The First Liberation: Contemplating Form With a Perception of Light

items.zh: 云何有色觀諸色？謂生欲界，已離欲界欲，未離色界欲。彼於如是所解脫中已得解脫，即於欲界諸色，以有光明相作意思惟，而生勝解。由二因緣，名為有色。謂生欲界故，得色界定故。又於有光明而作勝解故。
items.en: What is "having form, one contemplates forms"? One born in the desire realm who has left desire-realm desire but not form-realm desire: having already gained release within what is thus to be released, he attends to and contemplates desire-realm forms with a mark of luminosity, and generates a firm conviction. For two reasons it is called "having form": because he is born in the desire realm, and because he has attained a form-realm concentration; and also because he generates conviction towards luminosity.

items.zh: 問：觀諸色者，觀何等色？復以何行？答：欲界諸色。於諸勝處所制少色，若好、若惡、若劣、若勝；如是於多、乃至廣說。何故修習如是觀行？為淨修治能引最勝功德方便。何等名為最勝功德？謂勝處、遍處、諸聖神通、無諍、願智、無礙解等。雖先於彼欲界諸色已得離欲，然於彼色未能證得勝解自在。為證得故，數數於彼思惟勝解。
items.en: Question: In contemplating forms, what forms does he contemplate, and by what practice? Answer: Desire-realm forms — the lesser forms controlled by the [eight] masteries, whether good or bad, inferior or superior; and likewise the many forms, and so on at length. Why cultivate such a contemplation? To purify the path that can elicit the supreme qualities. What are the supreme qualities? The [eight] masteries, the [ten] totalities, the noble superknowledges, non-contention, the knowledge-of-vows, the analytic knowledges, and the rest. Although he has already left desire for those desire-realm forms, he has not yet attained sovereign conviction over them; in order to attain it, he repeatedly contemplates them with conviction.

items.title: The Second and Third Liberations: Contemplating External Form, and the "Pure Liberation"

items.zh: 云何內無色想觀外諸色？謂生欲界，已離色界欲，無色界定不現在前，又不思惟彼想明相，但於外色而作勝解。若於是色已得離欲，說彼為外。由二因緣，名內無色想。謂已證得無色等至，亦自了知得此定故，不思惟內光明相故。餘如前說。
items.en: What is "inwardly perceiving no form, one contemplates external forms"? One born in the desire realm who has left form-realm desire, whose formless attainment is not [taken as] present, who moreover does not contemplate that [internal] mark of luminosity, but generates conviction only towards external forms. Whatever form one has already left desire for is called "external." For two reasons it is called "inwardly perceiving no form": because he has attained a formless attainment and himself knows he has attained it, and because he does not contemplate the internal mark of luminosity. The rest is as stated before.

items.zh: 云何淨解脫身作證具足住？謂如有一，已得捨念圓滿清白，以此為依、修習清淨聖行圓滿；名淨解脫。何以故？三因緣故。謂已超過諸苦樂故，一切動亂已寂靜故，善磨瑩故。身作證者，於此住中，一切賢聖多所住故。
items.en: What is the pure liberation directly realised in the body and dwelt in complete? Someone who has attained the perfected, pure, and bright equanimity-and-mindfulness [of the fourth dhyāna] and, resting on this, cultivates to completion the pure noble practice — this is called the pure liberation. Why? For three reasons: because he has passed beyond all pain and pleasure, because all agitation is already stilled, and because [the mind] is well polished. "Directly realised in the body" means that all the worthy and noble ones abide much in this dwelling.

items.title: The Four Formless Liberations: Making the Boundless Attainments Sovereign

items.zh: 云何空無邊處解脫？謂如有一，於彼空處已得離欲，即於虛空思惟勝解。如是識無邊處解脫，於彼識處已得離欲，即於是識思惟勝解。無所有處解脫者，謂已得無所有處，於識無邊處思惟勝解。有頂解脫，更不於餘而作勝解；乃至遍於想可生處，即於是處應作勝解。
items.en: What is the liberation of the sphere of infinite space? Someone who has left desire for the space-sphere and generates conviction towards space itself. Likewise the liberation of the sphere of infinite consciousness: having left desire for the consciousness-sphere, he generates conviction towards that consciousness. The liberation of the sphere of nothingness: having attained the sphere of nothingness, he generates conviction towards the sphere of infinite consciousness [as being nothing]. The liberation of the peak of existence no longer generates conviction towards the other [spheres]; reaching everywhere that perception can arise, he generates conviction just there.

items.zh: 復次，先已修治作意勝解、後方能起勝知勝見，故名勝處。此勝當知復有五種。一、形奪卑下，故名為勝。謂如有一，以己勝上工巧等事，形奪他人置下劣位。二、制伏羸劣、故名為勝。謂如有一，以己強力摧諸劣者。三、能隱蔽他，故名為勝。謂瓶盆等能有覆障，或諸藥草呪術神通有所隱蔽。四、厭壞所緣，故名為勝。謂厭壞境界，捨諸煩惱。

items.title: The Eight Masteries: When the Mind Grows Stronger Than the Object

items.zh: 五、自在迴轉，故名為勝。謂世君王，隨所欲為處分臣僕。於此義中、意顯隱蔽及自在勝。前解脫中勝解自在，今於勝處制伏自在。
items.en: Fifth, because of sovereign turning [of the object] it is called "mastery" — as a worldly king disposes of his ministers and servants at will. … In this sense, what is highlighted is the mastery of concealment and of sovereignty: in the liberations there was sovereign conviction; here in the masteries there is sovereign subdual.

items.zh: 觀色少者，謂諸有情資具等色。觀色多者，謂諸宮殿房舍等色。言好色者，謂美妙顯色。一向淨妙故。與此相違，名為惡色。言劣色者，謂聲、香、味、觸不可意色。與此相違，當知勝色。此四顯色，有情資具、宮殿等攝。言勝知者，謂數數隱蔽所緣勝解。有如是想者，謂有制伏想也。
items.en: "Contemplating little form" means the forms of beings and their possessions; "contemplating much form" means the forms of palaces, houses, and the like. "Good form" means a beautiful visible colour, wholly fine; the opposite is "bad form." "Inferior form" means displeasing sound, scent, taste, and touch; the opposite, know, is "superior form." "Sovereign knowing" means repeatedly concealing the object of conviction. "Having such a perception" means having a perception of subdual.

items.title: The Ten Totalities: Pervading Everywhere Without a Boundary

items.zh: 復次，由諸遍處、於勝解事生遍勝解，故名遍處。言無二者，謂諸賢聖無我、我所二差別故。言無量者，遍一切故。
items.en: Furthermore, because of the totalities, one generates a pervasive conviction towards the object of conviction, so they are called "totalities." "Non-dual" means that the worthy and noble ones have no duality of self and mine. "Immeasurable" means pervading everywhere.

items.zh: 何故遍處唯就色、觸二處建立？由此二種，共自他身，遍有色界，常相續故。眼等根色唯屬自身，香、味二塵不遍一切；聲聲有間，是故不說如是有色諸遍處。定色界後邊，於無色中，空遍一切，故立遍處。
items.en: Why are the totalities established only on the form-base and the touch-base? Because these two, shared by one's own and others' bodies, pervade every realm that has form and are constantly continuous. The eye-faculty and the rest belong only to one's own body; scent and taste do not pervade everywhere; sound is intermittent — therefore such totality-concentrations are not stated for them. At the far edge of the form realm, within the formless, space pervades everything, so a totality is established [on it].

blocks.text: Today describes three classical sets of advanced meditations: the eight liberations, the eight masteries, and the ten totalities. They are less familiar to Western readers than the dhyānas, but they were standard in Indian Buddhism and are the basis of the supernormal powers. The commentary explains what each set is for.

The first liberation contemplates form "with a mark of luminosity". Venerable Miào Jìng: it arises from skeleton contemplation; one imagines light radiating from the skull between the brows. It leads to qualities that include the **analytic knowledges**, which, he notes, a teacher needs: "having attained the path and wanting to save beings widely, one still faces language problems."

In the second liberation, the skeleton is gone and only light is contemplated: "no inner form". The third is the "**pure liberation**", contemplating a beautiful object without being drawn by it. One reason for its name is 善磨瑩, "well polished". Venerable Miào Jìng: "like polishing a mirror; there's grime on it; grind it off, and gradually it shines." What is polished is the mind's clinging, not the object.
The sequence uses ugliness first, then beauty, to break the same attachment in two ways (Day 76): first by seeing the body's impurity, then by seeing beauty without desire.

The next four make the formless attainments into liberations: one who has left desire for each sphere generates conviction towards it. Venerable Miào Jìng on "nothingness": "use a wall to show that where there is no wall is empty"; nothingness is named from consciousness being absent. On "neither perception nor non-perception": it lacks sharp perception, so "not perception", yet faint perception remains, so "not non-perception".

The **eight masteries** (八勝處) are called mastery, Master Cháng Bǎi says, because "contemplation matures; mind grows strong and object weak; every object follows the mind". The meditator contemplates forms small and large, beautiful and ugly, and of the four colours, and masters them. Venerable Miào Jìng: "sovereign knowing" is calm, which repeatedly conceals the visualised field; "sovereign seeing" is insight, which calls it up again.

The **ten totalities** (十遍處, *kṛtsna*): earth, water, fire, wind, blue, yellow, red, white, space, and consciousness, each expanded to pervade everything "without a boundary". They are "non-dual": "the worthy and noble ones have no duality of self and mine." Why only form and touch? Because these are shared by self and others, pervade the form realm, and continue unbroken; the faculties are one's own, and smell and taste do not exist in the form realm.

Venerable Miào Jìng gives the sequence: the liberations come first, elicit the masteries, which elicit the totalities. Each step increases the mind's power over its objects. In Yogācāra terms, this is practical evidence for the main thesis: what appears as an object can be reshaped by the mind that presents it.

quiz.q: The first liberation attends with "a mark of luminosity." Where does Venerable Miào Jìng say this light arises?
options: from skeleton contemplation — imagining light radiating from the skull between the brows
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The mark of light is at the skeleton's skull, between the brows — one imagines light radiating from there." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*: one contemplates light to remove obstacles to transformation, not to remove craving.

quiz.q: In the second liberation, how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "inwardly no form" and "external"?
options: the skeleton is gone, only light is contemplated — no inner form; since one no longer clings to self or mine, it is called external
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Now the skeleton is gone — 'no inner form' — only light is contemplated"; "since one no longer grasps it as self or mine, it isn't called inner but outer." Master Cháng Bǎi lists four interpretations here.

quiz.q: The liberation of nothingness generates conviction towards the consciousness-sphere. Why, and what simile does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
options: as a wall reveals the empty space where there's no wall, so "nothingness" takes its name from consciousness being absent
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Use a wall to show that where there's no wall is empty; use a mountain to show where there's no mountain is empty." Master Cháng Bǎi: "The sphere of nothingness takes 'consciousness is nothing' as its own name."

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "neither perception" in the peak of existence?
options: lacking sharp perception is "not perception," yet it isn't no-perception — faint, dim perception remains
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The neither-perception sphere lacks sharp perception, hence 'not perception'; but it isn't 'no perception' — subtle, dim perception remains." Master Cháng Bǎi: "not-perception" means freed from the perceptions of the three lower spheres.

quiz.q: Why are the eight masteries called "mastery," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: contemplation matures; mind grows strong and object weak; every object follows the mind — it subdues the object
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Now contemplation is mature — mind strong, object weak; all objects turn as the mind wills; it subdues the object — hence 'mastery over the object.'" The text: like a king disposing of his servants at will.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what does "non-dual" mean in the totalities?
options: the worthy and noble have no duality of self and mine
quiz.why: "'Non-dual' means that the worthy and noble ones have no duality of self and mine. 'Immeasurable' means pervading everywhere." Master Cháng Bǎi: practising the totalities, the noble don't grasp the forms as self or mine.

quiz.q: Why are the totalities established only on form and touch?
options: form and touch are shared by self and others, pervade the form realm, and continue; faculties are one's own, scent and taste don't pervade, sound is intermittent
quiz.why: "Because these two, shared by one's own and others' bodies, pervade the form realm and are constantly continuous. The eye-faculty and the rest belong only to one's own body; scent and taste do not pervade everywhere; sound is intermittent." Master Cháng Bǎi: scent and taste exist only in the desire realm.
